correctness.rationale: For the balancing matrix M=[[6,-1],[1,0]], direct multiplication gives M^3=-I+5A with A integral. Binomial lifting yields M^(3*5^r)=-I+5^(r+1)A_r. Five successive shifts of length 3*5^r cancel their first-order coefficient modulo 5^(r+2), proving T_(r+1)(n)=5T_r(n) modulo 5^(r+2) for every even d, including d divisible by 5. Modulo 5 the even-power sequence repeats (0,1,1); hence T_0(n)=2 modulo 5. Induction and block concatenation yield S_(d,k)(n)=2k/3 modulo 5^(v5(k)+1) for 3|k, a nonzero residue on that valuation shell. If 3 does not divide k, comparing adjacent window sums modulo 5 yields a window with unit value. Executed standard-library checker made 6300 tests, including complete finite window-gcd comparisons and 5-adic lifting cases, recorded in verification-output.txt. Infinite result follows from symbolic identities, not the test count.

value.rationale: Mbirika–Schrader–Spilker ask for balancing-sequence sliding-window gcds; the power family extends a motivated arithmetic invariant beyond the previously treated squares. The first rank-three prime 5 is intrinsic to B_3=35 and the cube of the recurrence matrix. The theorem determines the complete 5-primary gcd for all positive window lengths and every positive even exponent and strengthens it to a uniform nonzero residue on the exact valuation shell for every start. This includes even exponents divisible by five where simple derivative invertibility fails; it is not an arbitrary modulus/parameter census. Other primes and odd exponents remain open in this result.
